### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **72** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/package.json`, `packages/cloud-connection/src/index.ts`, `packages/cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**61** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/package.json`, `packages/cloud-connection/src/index.ts`, `packages/cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **28** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f7e3a41b8a48c2618fd4a83249a8196794f0af35` — the merge of head `e17ecdb002c073cfed9d952080997c40acbded5e` into base `69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin f7e3a41b8a48c2618fd4a83249a8196794f0af35 && git checkout f7e3a41b8a48c2618fd4a83249a8196794f0af35
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4 e17ecdb002c073cfed9d952080997c40acbded5e && git checkout -B drift-repro 69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4 && git merge --no-ff e17ecdb002c073cfed9d952080997c40acbded5e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69244406b7e93b8856f3a5991ec18433a7e96dc4
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2117334321422ee0392cddbd5a45a1e42108039b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/cloud-connection/src/sys-cloud-binding-credential.object.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/connection-credential-ledger.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/connection-credential-preboot.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts

Inputs: card #31554 (body, claim 6722773582, os-dev-report 6723815310), parent cloud#3814 ruling table (comment 6722625146, R1–R6), PR body, the 17-file list and the net diff of `21173343` against `main` (merge-base `6f9f0086`), and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read in the live tree, never reviewed: `service-cluster/split-brain-guard.ts`, `objectql` `engine-secret-internal-fields.ts`, `engine-secrets-and-routing.ts` (datasource steps 1–5), `engine-update-dispatch.ts`, `engine-registration.ts`, `plugin.ts` (manifest service, `syncRegisteredSchemas` in `start()`), `core/kernel-base.ts`, `platform-objects/plugin.ts`, `spec` `stack.zod.ts` and `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, the cloud host's `artifact-kernel-factory.ts` (the `cloud` datasource alias).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Published spec accept-set widens** — `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE` gains the group `'cloud-connection': ['sys_cloud_binding_credential']`, so `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` and `isPlatformProvidedObjectName` accept one more name. Consumers read: `stack.zod.ts` now admits a top-level action whose `objectName` is this object (refused at boot where no package registers it, as for every other platform name); `@objectstack/lint` reference rules stop warning on it; `resolvePrimaryDatasource` skips names not registered in the deployment, so a single node is unaffected; `SECURITY_SURFACE_OBJECTS` reads only the `plugin-security` group. The conformance test derives the owning package from the path (`packages/cloud-connection/src/…` → `cloud-connection`). Right.
2. **`@objectstack/cloud-connection` public surface widens** — 12 value exports (`SysCloudBindingCredential`, `SharedConnectionCredentialLedger`, `SharedCredentialUnavailableError`, `fileCredentialLedger`, `sharesCloudBindingCredential`, `readCloudBindingCredentialBeforeBoot`, and the six constants) and 5 types; `CloudConnectionPluginConfig.sharedCredentialRefreshMs`; the plugin gains `optionalDependencies`, `destroy` and a second `providesServices` entry; one new kernel service `cloud-binding-credential` (shape `CloudBindingCredentialReader`), registered on every path because ADR-0116 `providesServices` is unconditional — on a single node it is a passive reader over the same file. Right.
3. **Wire** — `POST /api/v1/cloud-connection/bind/poll` gains a `503 ENVIRONMENT_BIND_FAILED` arm on shared replicas only; the code is already a row of `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` (its 502 arm), so no new code. Single node answers as before. Right.
4. **Storage** — one new table, created by ObjectQL's `start()` schema sync on replicas that registered the object at `init()`; one `sys_secret` handle per bind, released by the engine on rotate (`update` to a new value or `null`) and on `clear()` (`delete`). Right.
5. **Dependency graph** — `@objectstack/cloud-connection` takes `@objectstack/service-cluster` at runtime (no reverse edge: service-cluster does not depend on cloud-connection); `driver-sql`, `platform-objects`, `service-settings` are dev-only for the real-engine suites. Right.
6. **`@objectstack/cli`** — one `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_INVENTORY` row (`PMAIN`, `column-drop`, D7), the shape of `sys_presence` / `sys_platform_setting`; `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json` regenerated (+1 registered, +1 out of reach, +1 `systemFields.tenant: false`). Right.
7. **Metadata protocol** — nothing an author writes changes: the object is engine-owned, `apiEnabled: false`, not authorable. `none` is right.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/31554-cloud-binding-credential-shared.md`: `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/cli` at **patch**; none is `private`. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: a widening with kind `none` ships `patch`. Matches the diff (judgments 1, 2, 6). `@objectstack/service-cluster` is unchanged and needs none; `pnpm-lock.yaml` moves workspace links only. **(e) holds: `yes (widening)` is the correct declaration**; the dev's open question (A keep `no` / B re-declare) was answered B at `d3566fb1` and `21173343`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev `open_questions[0]`** (Clause-② re-declare): answered B, carried on both carriers. The card's claim comment 6722773582 still reads `Clause-②: no` — stale, not false in effect; see nit N1.
- **File surface beyond the claim** (`spec`, `cli`, census json, pinned engine-double ledger, docs, changeset, lockfile): each is forced by a conformance test or by delivery; stated in the PR body's Acceptance notes. Accepted.
- **Residual `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`** reads its own file store: outside this card by R6 (install-local refuses under declared replicas), separate card. Accepted.
- **Single-node file in the container layer**: maintainer question, deliberately not folded in. Accepted.
- **Cloud half (after the pin), for the #3814 PM thread**: (i) the pre-boot reader derives the driver from `OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER` unless the host passes `clusterDriver`; `os serve` reads that same variable (`serve.ts:3090`), so the default agrees — a host that configures the cluster driver in code must pass `clusterDriver`; (ii) the host must hand the same crypto provider the kernel installs (`envCrypto.provider` in `artifact-kernel-factory.ts`); (iii) a deployment that manages DDL out of band (`OS_SKIP_SCHEMA_SYNC=1`) must create `sys_cloud_binding_credential` itself, as for any platform object — `os serve` and the cloud artifact kernel (outside repair mode) sync by default.
- **Docs face (lane seat's sentence check, not this record's)**: `cloud-connection.mdx` says an online licence check "sees a change within 30 seconds" — true once the cloud half reads `cloud-binding` or `cloud-binding-credential`; forward-looking today.
- **Author**: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note owed.
- **Check-runs on `21173343` at review time (16:41Z)**: Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates, every Lint · lane, Type Check · source gates and · debt ledger, Spec property liveness, Validate Package Dependencies, Build UI Deps / Docs / E2E UI, Live E2E UI all `success`; Build Core, Test Core 1–8, Test UI 1–16, Type Check · workspace and · consumer gates still `in_progress`. The queue reads their conclusions at enqueue.

### ④ Design judgment

**(a) R3 holds — single node and every non-Redis driver untouched.** `chooseLedger()` returns the file ledger when `declaresMultiNode(process.env)` is false, and again when the cluster service's `driver` (`IClusterService.driver`, the string `defineCluster` parsed) is anything but `redis` (`sharesCloudBindingCredential`). On those paths nothing is registered with `manifest`, nothing is logged, and `fileCredentialLedger` is a one-to-one pass-through over the unchanged `ConnectionCredentialStore` — every former `this.store.read()/write()/clear()` call site now goes through it with the same arguments, `door()` mounts handlers bare when `ledger.shared` is false, and `createCloudBinding` reads the same `read()`. The predicate is service-cluster's own, so the split-brain guard, cloud#3880 and this ledger cannot drift. The store suite pins four topologies (Redis with no declaration, declared over `memory`, declared over `postgres`, declared with no cluster service) to the exact pre-change bytes and mode `0600`, with no credential object registered. Holds.

**(b) Pre-boot reader.** `readCloudBindingCredentialBeforeBoot` returns `not-shared` before `openDriver` is called unless the same predicate holds; otherwise it opens one driver, builds a bare `ObjectQL`, `registerDriver(opened, true)`, registers the object under namespace `sys` with the plugin manifest's id (the same name and table the manifest path registers — the plugin test with a `cloud` datasource writes through `registerApp` and reads back here), sets the host's provider, and reads through the same `SharedConnectionCredentialLedger.load()` the plugin uses. No `syncSchemas`, no write. Every failure, including an open that throws, a first boot with no table, another key and a hung read, is `{ status: 'unavailable', reason }`; nothing throws; reasons carry the ledger's remedy text or an engine `find` fault the engine redacts (`redactPropagatedDriverFault`), never the token. The bare engine starts no timers (`engine*.ts` has no `setInterval`), so nothing outlives the call but the connection, which is disconnected. **One should-fix (S1)** on the bound, below.

**(c) Sealing, one decrypt path.** `runtime_token` is `Field.secret` (spec `data/field.zod.ts`): `encryptSecretFields` seals it with the engine's `cryptoProvider` into a `sys_secret` row written immediately before the record's own write, fail-closed with `Cannot persist secret field …` when no provider or no `sys_secret` store is reachable — which the ledger maps to `SharedCredentialUnavailableError` and the shared `/bind/poll` arm to 503, storing nothing (pinned). Reads mask the column (`maskSecretFields`), and the only dereference is `resolveSecretField`, used by `credentialOf` on both the plugin and the pre-boot path. The engine refuses `''` in a secret column and clears on `null`, so the ledger writes `token || null`; the old handle is released on rotate and on delete (`releaseSecretHandles`, `deletedSecretSlots`). `withoutToken` scrubs a driver message that echoed the value; the ledger's and plugin's own messages carry no value; the two-process suite checks the database file, both logs and both stderr streams for the bearer. `access: { default: 'private' }` (ADR-0066), `apiEnabled: false` with `apiMethods: []` (REST `enforceApiAccess`), `managedBy: 'engine-owned'` and `isSystem` mirror `sys_connector_credential`, the existing `secret`-field precedent. The ledger's `update({ id, …columns })` and `delete({ where: { id } })` are the by-id shapes `resolveEngineUpdateDispatch` / `resolveEngineDeleteDispatch` accept; the insert race on the global unique `slot` index is caught by `DUPLICATE_RECORD` and replayed as an update. Holds.

**(d) Default datasource, beside `sys_secret`.** The manifest registered at `init()` names no `defaultDatasource` (the 21173343 fix). Routing (`engine-secrets-and-routing.ts` steps 1–5) for `sys_cloud_binding_credential` and for `sys_secret` reads the same inputs: no object-level `datasource`, no datasource mapping entry, no `lifecycle.class`, and an owning manifest with no `defaultDatasource` (platform-objects' main manifest names none; only its activation-ledger manifest says `cloud`) — so both fall to step 5, the default driver, on any host, including the cloud host that registers the `cloud` alias. The pinned case with a second `cloud` driver shows `getDriverForObject` answering the primary for both, the row and its handle landing on the primary, no table on `cloud`, and the pre-boot read finding it with one connection to the primary. Registration timing is right: the manifest `register` runs in cloud-connection's `init()`, hoisted after ObjectQL and the cluster plugin by `optionalDependencies` (ADR-0116 order-if-present), and the kernel runs every `init` before any `start`, so `syncRegisteredSchemas` in ObjectQL's `start()` creates the table before `kernel:ready` reads it. Holds.

**`platform-object-names.ts` (hits).** The new group's jsdoc states the condition (registered only with replicas declared over Redis). Conditional registration is already this registry's semantics — `plugin-audit`'s objects exist only when that plugin is composed — and the one consumer that would mind an absent object (`resolvePrimaryDatasource`) skips names the registry does not hold. The ruling it implements (cloud#3814 R2/R3, the PM thread's database-row choice over KV) and its first consumer (the conformance test, then the census and inventory) agree. Holds.

**Plugin freshness.** Doors re-read the row per request (`door` → `refreshShared`); the synchronous `cloud-binding` service answers the copy of the last load, refreshed at `kernel:ready` and every 30 s, stopped on `kernel:shutdown` and `destroy()`; a failed re-read keeps the last copy and is reported once per distinct message at `error` with the remedy, never as "unbound". `adoptFrom` moves a single node's file into an empty row once and leaves the file. Matches the contract the module header states.

**Findings**

- **S1 — should-fix — the pre-boot bound is stated as one shared budget; the code grants the close a second full one.** `connection-credential-preboot.ts`: the docblock says "open, read and close share one time bound" and `timeoutMs` is documented as "the bound on open, read and close together"; the PR body, changeset and docs repeat "3 seconds by default". The code races open + read against `timeoutMs`, then in `finally` awaits `boundedClose(close(), timeoutMs)` with a fresh timer, so a slow `disconnect()` after a successful or failed read holds the boot for up to 2 × `timeoutMs`. And on the timeout path the close is started (`void close()`), not awaited, so "disconnected before this returns, on every path" is "initiated" there. Result correctness is untouched; the licence gate's boot budget is what is overstated. Fix either way: pass the remaining budget (`deadline - Date.now()`, floor 0) to `boundedClose`, and say "initiated" for the timeout path; or keep the code and state the real bound (up to twice `timeoutMs`) in the docblock, the changeset and `cloud-connection.mdx`. The first moves the head and takes a delta review by this reviewer; the second touches prose faces and the implementing file's jsdoc.
- **N1 — nit — card claim comment is stale.** Comment 6722773582 on #31554 still declares `Clause-②: no`; the PR body and changeset carry `yes (widening)`. The seat posts a one-line superseding declaration on the card (prose, no head move).
- **N2 — nit — `withoutToken` scrubs `Error` instances only.** A driver or provider that throws a non-`Error` value echoing its input would carry the bearer into the plugin's `error` line. No shipped driver does; an accepted deviation, or `String(err)` scrubbing in a later round.
- **N3 — nit — per-request re-read on shared doors.** Each `/api/v1/cloud-connection/*` request costs a row read, a `sys_secret` read and a decrypt. The routes are Setup-page admin calls; the contract names the re-read on purpose. Accepted deviation.

Implemented-by: `session_01QUs3BuscNGgAkKzuN3beuN`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QUs3BvRfC6NV59qZLKnMoE`

**VERDICT: PASS**

One should-fix (S1) and three nits; no must-fix. A fix for S1 that moves the head owes a delta review of the fix by this reviewer; nits alone end the round.

### ④ Design judgment

**`connection-credential-preboot.ts` against its stated contract.** The docblock now says: one deadline taken when the call starts; the open and the read race it; the close gets only the budget left, at least 50 ms (`PREBOOT_CLOSE_FLOOR_MS`) when the read answers at the very end; the call returns within the bound or within that floor after it; on the timeout path the disconnect is initiated and not awaited; a late open is closed the moment it lands. The code, read line by line:

- `deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs` is computed after the `not-shared` short-circuit and before `attempt` starts, so the open is inside the budget from its first tick.
- The race timer is `setTimeout(…, Math.max(deadline - Date.now(), 0))`, so open plus read cannot run past the deadline.
- In `finally`, `boundedClose(close(), Math.max(deadline - Date.now(), PREBOOT_CLOSE_FLOOR_MS))`: a close after a quick read gets nearly the whole budget; a close after a read that answered at the end gets 50 ms; a hung `disconnect()` is left initiated in both cases. Total ≤ `timeoutMs` + 50 ms, as the docblock and the option doc state.
- The timeout path is unchanged in behaviour (`void close()`, `attempt.catch` so no unhandled rejection) and its comment and the docblock now say "initiated".
- The late-open path (`if (abandoned) { await close(); throw … }`) is unchanged and still closes the connection when it lands.

**Changeset and docs sentences the fix rewrote** (prose faces; the lane seat's sentence check owns them, read here because S1 named them). **Findings**

- **N4 — nit — one changeset clause overstates by the floor.** `.changeset/31554-cloud-binding-credential-shared.md`: "so a hung disconnect never holds the boot past the bound" is exact for the timeout path; on the read-answered path a hung disconnect can hold the boot up to the 50 ms floor past the bound, which the same sentence's "at least 50 ms" already implies. Prose face; the lane seat may tighten it to "past the bound by more than the 50 ms floor" or accept it as written.
- **N5 — nit — wall-clock bound tests.** As in ③: 500 ms slack on a 2500 ms cut. Accepted as written; flaky-case rules if it reds.

No must-fix, no should-fix; nits alone end the round for this head.
